title: Black Pepper Tofu
description: Ottolenghi's legendary tofu dish — crispy cubes bathed in a buttery, fiery sauce loaded with shallots, chillies, and a frankly reckless amount of black pepper. Vegetarian but nobody will miss the meat.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: for frying, enough to coat the pan generously

ingredients.name: shallots
ingredients.notes: about 350g total, peeled and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: black peppercorns
ingredients.notes: coarsely crushed in a mortar or under a pan

steps.text: Cut the tofu into roughly 3x2cm cubes. Toss in cornstarch, shake off the excess. Heat a generous layer of oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu in batches until golden and crusty on all sides. Transfer to paper towels to drain.
steps.tip: Press the tofu dry with paper towels before cubing — less moisture means crispier edges.

steps.text: Wipe out the pan and discard the frying oil. Melt the butter over low-medium heat. Add the shallots, chillies, garlic, and ginger. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until completely soft and glossy, about 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Patience here. You're melting the shallots down, not browning them. Keep the heat gentle.

steps.text: Add the sweet soy sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar. Stir to combine. Add the crushed black peppercorns.
Return the fried tofu to the pan and toss gently to warm through and coat in the sauce, about 1 minute. Fold in the scallion segments.

steps.tip: This dish is meant to be fiery. If you want to dial back the heat, reduce the chillies and peppercorns — but the whole point is the burn.
